Donald Barr hired Epstein (Barr's last day June 30, 1974); Peter Branch was interim headmaster July 1-Dec 31, 1974; Gardner Dunnan headmaster Jan 1, 1975-June 30, 1997. In US v. Epstein (96 CIV 8307, SDNY 1998), the US Government sued to evict Epstein from a building formerly used as the residence of the Deputy Consul General of Iran. After diplomatic relations were severed in 1980, OFM leased the building to Epstein in 1992. Epstein sublet it to attorney Ivan S. Fisher in 1996 without consent. Government terminated Epsteins lease and sought ejectment plus back rent. Epstein was represented by Wachtel & Masyr LLP (Steven J. Cohen). Judge Chin presided.

Seymour Epstein family economics (NYC Municipal Archives): Volscho pulled Seymour G. Epstein's salary from NYC Civil Lists 1969-1981. Address: 3814 Sea Gate Avenue, Brooklyn (moved from 3742 Maple Ave between 1974-75). Parks Department employee, earned $13,530 in 1975 (weekly earnings slightly below Brooklyn median for white male 54-64 per 1970 Census). Final salary $18,000 in 1981 ($62K in 2024 dollars). Retired 1983 after two heart attacks. Jeffrey's Dalton salary (~$12,000) roughly matched his father's earnings in 1974 — the year Jeffrey started teaching. The coincident timing of the family's move (1974-75) with Jeffrey's new income suggests he may have been contributing to household finances. Seymour wrote: 'I enjoyed working for the park dept' and 'worked in every park in district 9.'

Incorporation done by Freehold NJ law firm Sonnenblick Parker and Selvers.

In Stroll v. Epstein (818 F.Supp. 640, SDNY 1993, Judge Conboy), Michael R. Stroll sued Epstein over a 1984 contract. Epstein and Stroll had entered a joint venture in 1982 via Intercontinental Asset Group (I.A.G.). Epstein served as officer of I.A.G. and agent for the venture. The November 1984 contract addressed Strolls rescission of his interest. Court granted Epsteins summary judgment, finding he acted in representative capacity for I.A.G. This predates Gold & Wachtel representation but establishes Epsteins 1982-era business entity.

34 E 69th St property scheme details: Epstein leased the former Iranian Deputy Consul General residence from the Office of Foreign Missions (US State Department) on Feb 1, 1992 at $15K/month. The lease required single-family residential use by Epstein and advance WRITTEN permission for any subletting. Epstein extended the lease through Jan 31, 1997 and received right of first refusal. In Jan 1996, Epstein abandoned the premises. In March 1996, he negotiated simultaneously with Xenophon Galinas (who offered $100K for improvements) and Fisher. Meanwhile, OFM negotiated directly with Galinas for a new lease at $16K/month from Feb 1997. On Apr 16, 1996 Epstein tried to exercise right of first refusal; on Apr 26, 1996 OFM denied sublease to Fisher. Despite denial, Epstein entered sublease with Fisher on May 7, 1996 at $20K/month — netting Epstein $5K/month profit from a government-custodied Iranian diplomatic property. He also claimed to own Iranian government fixtures (chandeliers, sconces, mirrors). Government filed suit Nov 1996; lease terminated Aug 23, 1996. Epstein represented by Steven J. Cohen of Wachtel & Masyr LLP (now Wachtel Missry).

34 E 69th St (former Iranian deputy consul general residence) was Epstein's NYC home from Feb 1992 to Jan 1996 before he moved to 9 E 71st St. Epstein leased from the State Department's Office of Foreign Missions at K/month, extended in Aug 1992 for 3 additional years with right of first refusal. He abandoned the property in January 1996 but continued paying rent and attempted to monetize it through subletting. Property was Iranian government property held under the Foreign Missions Act. The lease was terminated Aug 23, 1996. This establishes Epstein's pre-71st Street NYC residence and his relationship with the US State Department as landlord. Judge Denny Chin (later elevated to 2d Circuit) presided over the ejectment case.

Even if Dalton destroyed personnel records they could have retrieved yearbooks showing Epstein as teacher. SYNTHESIS: Epstein may have used the threat of forced withdrawal from DB Zwirn (17:1 leverage, illiquid assets) as leverage during NPA plea negotiations. Timeline correlation: withdrawal demands (Nov 2006-June 2008) map directly onto NPA negotiation period. Schulte Roth denied withdrawal March 27, 2007 but the threat itself created pressure on Zwirn, Dubin, and other LPs. 'Withdrawal Requests Not Sent' (documents missing as of Jan 28 2010) suggest demands were drafted and held back — loaded guns for negotiation rather than actual redemption attempts. Dubin's affidavit on 'Zwirn liquidity' provided expert ammunition on fund fragility. At 17:1 leverage, a large forced redemption during 2007-2008 credit crisis could trigger cascade failures. Key stakeholders with incentive to prevent this: Dan Zwirn (fund survival), Glen Dubin (reputation/exposure), other LPs, and regulators who wanted no additional fund blowups during financial crisis. Pattern: Epstein using financial positions as leverage in criminal defense negotiations, not just for investment returns.

findings.summary: Jeffrey Epstein has ZERO appearances in Senate LDA records as either a client or a lobbyist. No Epstein-named entity (LSJE LLC, Southern Trust Company, Financial Trust Company) appears as a lobbying client. This confirms Epstein's influence operations were conducted entirely outside the formal lobbying disclosure framework - through nonprofits (IPI, HDI, Gratitude America), personal relationships, legal representation disguised as counsel, and financial payments rather than registered lobbying contacts.

KEY ANALYTICAL QUESTION: What was the 'Softbank caper' that Weingarten referenced? The term 'caper' implies an active operation, not mere legal representation. Combined with Epstein's 'go slow' advice and instruction to 'get the book on him' (gather intelligence), this suggests Epstein and Weingarten were contemplating involvement in or exploitation of the SoftBank situation — possibly: (1) Representing Misra while gathering compromising intelligence on him, (2) Representing the TARGETS of Misra's smear campaign, (3) Inserting themselves as intelligence brokers between factions, or (4) Running a parallel intelligence operation for an undisclosed client. The fact that Epstein immediately asked Teodorani about Benedetti 48 hours later — confirming he was researching the operative, not just the principal — suggests option 3 or 4: intelligence brokerage or parallel operation.

ASSESSMENT: Epstein as intelligence broker in SoftBank operation. The evidence supports a model where Epstein functioned as a PRIVATE INTELLIGENCE HUB connecting multiple parties circling the SoftBank/Misra situation. The network topology on Jan 25-28, 2019: (1) Weingarten (Steptoe) asked Epstein about Misra — seeking to represent him or use him; (2) Karp (Paul Weiss) was already representing SoftBank and had spoken to Misra; (3) Epstein was the ONLY person who knew both Weingarten and Karp were both involved — he told Weingarten 'dont mention my role with brad'; (4) Epstein probed Teodorani about Benedetti — researching the operative; (5) Epstein knew Benedetti personally from Paris 2013; (6) Epstein had SoftBank intelligence from Gulf sources (Jabor), media (Thomas), and deal flow (Barrett). This is CLASSIC intelligence brokerage: Epstein sat at the intersection of legal, corporate, intelligence, and media networks, able to trade information between parties who did not know the others were involved. The 'go slow' and 'get the book on him' instructions show he was managing the engagement strategically, not merely connecting people.

Epstein's intelligence broker model exposed through the Jan 21-26, 2019 72-hour window. He simultaneously: (1) received SDNY RICO advance intelligence and shared it with Weingarten (Jan 21); (2) discussed the 'new guy' who 'could only shoot blanks' (Jan 22) — likely a potential new criminal defense attorney or cooperator; (3) told Karp about google/ghosen/SIC updates (Jan 24); (4) brokered Weingarten's introduction to SoftBank's Misra through Karp connection (Jan 25-26); (5) directed Weingarten to watch Masayoshi Son YouTube with 'eyes that I have opened for you' (Jan 26). This is classic intelligence tradecraft: collecting from multiple sources (DOJ, SDNY, corporate Japan), synthesizing, and distributing to parties who each received only partial information.

SYNTHESIS: The SoftBank honey trap operation (Benedetti-Misra, WSJ Feb 2020) maps directly to Epstein's documented coercion infrastructure. The primary corpus establishes: (1) Spy cameras purchased from stores and installed in Kleenex boxes (EFTA02580827, Feb 2014) with pattern going back to 2003 (EFTA02728545); (2) Maxwell coaching blackmail defense strategies (EFTA02434764, Dec 2009); (3) Epstein sending blackmail-related articles to his lawyers (EFTA02475670, EFTA02594252); (4) DNA collection from Gulf contacts including Jabor Al Thani, Sultan, and Alahmadi registered under controlled accounts (EFTA02324345, EFTA02224464); (5) Direct connection to Benedetti via Paris calendar (EFTA02297224, Sept 2013) and inquiry via Teodorani (EFTA02628256, Jan 28, 2019); (6) Knowledge of Misra's legal representation via Karp (EFTA02627134, Jan 26, 2019) -- just 2 days before the Benedetti inquiry. The timeline is: Epstein asks Karp about Misra (Jan 26), Epstein asks Teodorani about Benedetti (Jan 28), and Epstein was arrested 6 months later (July 6, 2019). Benedetti was the operative who orchestrated the SoftBank honey trap. Epstein was the node connecting Benedetti, Karp/Paul Weiss, the SoftBank intelligence from Jabor, and the surveillance tradecraft.

findings.summary: AML COMPLIANCE DIRECTOR-1 drafted internal memo on November 6, 2013 concluding 'basis for closure' of Danske Estonia accounts due to lack of AML improvement. Memo was never sent to any other DB personnel or third party prior to account closure in October 2015. Two days later on Nov 8, 2013, US AFC officers discussed concerns on call with German colleagues — Danske Estonia described as 'not cooperative enough' and had 'not improved.' AML COMPLIANCE DIRECTOR-1 then advocated maintaining relationship while mitigating risks.
findings.detail: By early 2014, other major Western financial institutions were de-risking the Baltic region. DB elected to continue. In Sept 2014 transition memo, AML COMPLIANCE DIRECTOR-1 stated: the Baltics suffer from an inherently high client AML risk. Continued monitoring should be placed on Danske Bank Estonia. If the situation worsens, I recommend that the account be closed. Despite this recommendation, DB continued relationship. DB maintained Danske Estonia because: (1) it was viewed as important component of global relationship with Danske Bank A/S, and (2) DB believed it could effectively mitigate and control the risks. Danske Estonia only began screening incoming payments against sanctions lists in 2014 — previously only screened outgoing. First change to client risk level determination procedures in five years occurred in 2014. Annual AML Discussions showed largely no changes year after year.
